why: A sorted sequence becomes a height-balanced BST by making the middle element the root and recursing on the left and right halves. The linked-list twist is that you re-point the existing prev/next fields as left/right instead of allocating tree nodes.
hints: In a balanced BST built from sorted values, which value is the root? The middle one, so half the values go each side.
Recurse on index ranges [lo, hi]: mid = (lo + hi) // 2 (the lower middle for even sizes), left = build(lo, mid - 1), right = build(mid + 1, hi), and set parent of both children to mid.
Use an explicit stack or rely on depth being only O(log n). Fill a [index, left, right, parent] row per node: O(n) time, O(n) for the output.
pitfalls: Even-sized segments must use the lower middle, (lo + hi) // 2, or the table will not match.
Every link not set must be -1, including the root's parent.
Walking the list to find each middle costs O(n log n); index arithmetic on the array avoids that.
